subject: Priv Infra: module slimming, CI merge window coordination
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@acmecloud.com
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Priv Infra: module slimming, CI merge window coordination

Team —

Following up from the infra sync: attached is a trimmed inventory of the private-deploy modules we currently have in the repo and a short note proposing a merge window for consolidation. High-level goals: reduce duplicate Terraform modules, align Helm values schema across services, and collapse overlapping Ansible roles so the air‑gap packaging step is simpler.

Key asks up front:
- Review the inventory sheet and mark any module you own that cannot be changed during the proposed window (see attached sheet).
- Confirm the CI changes in the MR (link below) can be staged during the 9/21-9/22 merge window.
- If you have critical e2e tests that must run pre-merge, list them so we can prioritize pipeline time.

Notes on constraints:
- ACME is still doing the on‑prem network maintenance 9/20–9/21; we should avoid rolling egress rules during that maintenance. I cc'd ops@acmecloud.com to flag that.
- Any module-level interface changes must provide backward-compatible input variables for at least two weeks.

Proposed timeline (subject to quick feedback):
- 9/15: freeze new feature MRs for priv modules (exceptions by approval)
- 9/21 02:00–10:00 UTC: merge window (staged, per-team rollouts)
- 9/21–9/23: canary → full promotion, with automated rollback policy in MR

Attachments: module-inventory-20270914.xlsx, proposed-merge-window-202709.md
Links: https://gitlab.redwoodinfra.com/redwood/priv-infra/-/merge_requests/482

Thanks — please reply with explicit "ok for merge window" or list blockers.

—
Marissa Cole
Sr Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, ops@acmecloud.com
Date: 2027-09-14T12:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Priv Infra: module slimming, CI merge window coordination

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear plan. Quick notes from infra:

1) Backwards compatibility and KV cache: any Terraform change that touches kvcache config (namespaces or TTL keys) must be staged behind a feature flag. We have customer-facing LROs that depend on exact cache keys; accidental renames will break read path.

2) Helm value schema: we should adopt a strict JSON Schema validator as part of the Helm lint stage. I pushed a small prototype in the MR (see pipeline diffs). If teams use the schema, we can fail fast on incompatible value shapes instead of discovering at runtime.

3) Network egress gating: ACME’s window overlaps our proposed dates; ops@acmecloud.com, can you confirm whether node egress ACLs will be modifiable on 9/21? If not, we need to move the traffic-related merges to 9/23.

4) Test matrix: we need at least one fast smoke test (30s) and one medium e2e (5–10m) per module. We should add a lightweight canary tag so the runner can prioritize these tests during the merge window.

I’ve annotated module-inventory with ownership notes and flagged two modules that must be preserved until release: priv-network-egress and vault-bootstrap.

Quoted for context:
> On 2027-09-14 09:12, Marissa Cole wrote:
> > Following up from the infra sync: attached is a trimmed inventory ...

Grace O'Connor
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@acmecloud.com
Date: 2027-09-14T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Priv Infra: module slimming, CI merge window coordination

Pushing a quick update — I opened the GitLab MR for the CI changes (MR 482) and added the pipeline diffs. CI notes:

- We introduced a new job group `priv:quick-smoke` that runs the 30s checks in parallel across modules.
- A second job `priv:canary-e2e` spins up a minimal on‑prem-like env (containerized network emulator + minikube profile) to run the 5–10m e2e tests. This lives behind a `canary` flag in the MR so it won't run on every push.
- The patch includes a gating condition that prevents merging if `priv:quick-smoke` fails.

GitLab MR: https://gitlab.redwoodinfra.com/redwood/priv-infra/-/merge_requests/482
Patch attached: ci-pipeline-diff.patch

Ops team — I added a deploy-note in the MR outlining the egress changes. If ACME cannot accept the 9/21 window for ACL edits, we can still proceed with schema/helm/role consolidations and schedule the egress changes for 9/23 as a follow-up.

Also FYI: I included a short forward from ACME (see below) confirming they want no node egress changes during their maintenance on 9/20–9/21.

---- Forwarded message ----
From: ACME On‑Prem Ops <ops@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2027-09-13T15:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Maintenance window 9/20–9/21
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai

Confirming: we will be performing network firmware updates 9/20–9/21 and prefer no ACL changes during that window.

---- end forwarded message ----

Priyom Das
Staff DevOps Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@acmecloud.com, sam.rivera@bigbank.com
Date: 2027-09-15T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Priv Infra: module slimming, CI merge window coordination

All —

Thanks for the quick turn. I agree with Grace and Priyom’s mitigations. Final call:

- Proceed with non-network consolidations during 9/21 merge window as planned (helm schema harmonization, Terraform module merging, Ansible role consolidation).
- Move explicit ACL/egress changes to 9/23 to respect ACME maintenance. Priyom — mark those MR commits with `egress:deferred` and we'll gate them behind a targeted rollout.
- Enforce the `priv:quick-smoke` gating job. If smoke fails, automerge is blocked and we triage within the hour.

Next steps:
- Marissa: publish the updated merge-window note that reflects the 9/23 egress fallback and share an updated checklist.
- Priyom: add `egress:deferred` tags and the canary rollout playbook to MR 482.
- Grace: land the JSON Schema validator into the helm lint stage (small MR ok to follow).

Ops@ACME: thanks for the heads-up — we’ll avoid ACL edits during your maintenance window and coordinate for 9/23 if that works.

I consider this approved pending the small MRs and the final checklist update.

—
Aditya Rao
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
